Zucchini and pear purée: Wash and peel the zucchini and pear; remove the pear core.
Cut both into small cubes.
Steam for 8 minutes, until easily mashed with a fork.
Blend until smooth; add cooking water if too thick.
Pear sweetens the mild taste of zucchini; no sugar needed.
In a closed container in the fridge for 24 hours; 1 month in an ice cube tray.
Cinnamon-free sweet potato and apple purée
3–4 tablespoons cooking water
Peel the sweet potato and apple; remove the apple core.
Cut into small cubes.
Steam the sweet potato for 10 minutes; add the apple and steam 5 more minutes.
You can add a pinch of cinnamon after 8 months.
Quinoa and pumpkin porridge
1 slice pumpkin (about 100 g)
Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve, rubbing under plenty of water; this removes bitterness.
Peel the pumpkin and cut into small cubes.
Bring the quinoa, pumpkin and water to a boil in a small pot.
Cook on low heat for 18 minutes, stirring now and then, until the quinoa is completely soft.
Quinoa is a grain alternative rich in iron and protein.
Beetroot and apple purée
1 small red beetroot
Peel the beetroot and apple; beetroot can stain hands, so wear gloves.
Cut into small cubes.
Steam the beetroot for 20 minutes; add the apple for the last 6 minutes.
Mix beetroot into yoghurt for a pink bowl.
Avocado spoon food with pear
Peel and core the pear; if firm, steam for 4 minutes to soften.
Scoop out the avocado with a spoon.
Mash both together with a fork until smooth.
Avocado provides healthy fat, pear provides fibre.
Strained lentil and carrot soup
Rinse the lentils until the water runs clear; peel and finely chop the carrot.
Blend, then pass through a fine sieve.
If giving lentils for the first time, start with a small amount; they can cause gas.
Salmon and broccoli mash
50 g boneless salmon
Peel and finely chop the potato; wash the broccoli.
Steam the potato for 8 minutes; add the broccoli and salmon and steam 8 more minutes.
Mash everything with a fork; small pieces can remain.
Salmon is rich in omega-3; fish is recommended 1–2 times a week.
Turkey meatballs (soft)
100 g minced turkey
Half a small zucchini (grated)
Knead the minced turkey, zucchini and oats; then wash your hands.
You can also shape the meatballs into sticks the baby can hold.
2 days in the fridge; 1 month in the freezer.
Chicken and quinoa mash
Rinse the quinoa by rubbing it; finely chop the carrot and chicken.
Bring everything to a boil with the water; skim off the foam.
Mash with a fork or blend briefly.
Quinoa and chicken together are a good source of protein.
Spinach mash with curd cheese
1 handful spinach leaves
Wash the spinach several times in plenty of water; peel and finely chop the potato.
Boil the potato for 10 minutes; add the spinach for the last 3 minutes.
Drain and mash with a fork; stir in the curd cheese.
Iron absorption from spinach improves with vitamin C-rich fruit.
Sweet potato lentil patties
Rinse the lentils and cook with 1 cup water for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed and they fall apart.
Steam the sweet potato for 12 minutes and mash.
Knead the lentils, sweet potato and oats; rest for 10 minutes.
Shape small flat patties and place on the tray; bake for 15 minutes.
A soft finger food for the baby to self-feed.
Zucchini egg muffins (baby)
Preheat the oven to 180°C; grease a mini muffin tin.
Whisk the eggs; add the zucchini and curd cheese.
Divide into the moulds and bake for 15 minutes, until the centre is completely set.
Egg is a common allergen; if giving it for the first time, start with a small amount.
Broccoli quinoa bites
3–4 broccoli florets
Boil the broccoli for 6 minutes and chop very finely.
Mix the quinoa, broccoli, egg and breadcrumbs; rest for 10 minutes.
If the bites fall apart, add 1 more spoon of breadcrumbs.
Vegetable chickpea patties (baked)
Remove the chickpea skins and mash well with a fork.
Add the carrot, oats and olive oil and knead.
You can serve with a yoghurt-dill sauce.
Zucchini cheese waffles
1 small zucchini (grated)
Whisk the egg, milk and flour until smooth; add the zucchini and kashar cheese.
Heat the waffle maker and grease lightly.
Pour in the batter and cook for 4–5 minutes, until golden.
Let cool and cut into strips the child can hold.
If you have no waffle maker, make small pancakes in a pan.
Turkey and vegetable pasta
50 g small pasta
80 g minced turkey
1 small tomato (grated)
Cook the mince in olive oil for 5 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon, until it has changed colour completely.
Add the zucchini and tomato and cook covered for 8 minutes.
Turkey is a lean, easily digested meat option.
